text: Connes' complex of cyclic cochains with the Hochschild coboundary, its cohomology HCⁿ(A; M) for a unital algebra A, with HC⁰ the traces, functorial along algebra homomorphisms (Connes, *Noncommutative Geometry*, III.1).

name: The field of Puiseux series
text: the union of the ramified levels K⸨t^{1/n}⸩ inside Hahn series with rational exponents is a field, each level has degree n over K⸨t⸩, and the whole field is algebraic over K⸨t⸩ in every characteristic (Walker, *Algebraic Curves*, Ch. IV).

name: Badly approximable numbers
text: the irrationals ξ with q‖qξ‖ bounded below by a positive constant; they have irrationality exponent 2, and every real quadratic irrational is badly approximable (Cassels, *An Introduction to Diophantine Approximation*, Ch. I).

name: The area formula
text: for a Lipschitz map f between finite-dimensional inner product spaces, ∫_A Jf·g dx = ∫ Σ_{x ∈ A ∩ f⁻¹(y)} g(x) dℋⁿ(y) for measurable A and g ≥ 0; with g = 1 the right side counts the fibre A ∩ f⁻¹(y) (Evans–Gariepy, *Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions*, §3.3).

name: Tits' theorem for BN-pairs
text: for every Tits system (G, B, N, S), the Weyl group W = N/(B ∩ N) with its simple reflections S is a Coxeter system, now in full after the exchange condition of TauCeti#9029 (Bourbaki, *Lie*, Ch. IV §2.4, Thm 2).

name: Adic completions of Noetherian rings are Noetherian
text: a ring that is complete for the adic topology of a finitely generated ideal I with R/I Noetherian is Noetherian; in particular the I-adic completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian for every ideal I (Atiyah–Macdonald, *Introduction to Commutative Algebra*, Thm 10.26).

name: The generator rank of a p-adic absolute Galois group
text: for a finite extension K of ℚ_p, the absolute Galois group G_K has exactly [K : ℚ_p] + 2 topological generators, sharpening the finite generation announced from TauCeti#17192 (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, *Cohomology of Number Fields*, (7.4.1)).

name: The homology of complex projective space
text: for any coefficient object R of an abelian category, H_k(ℂPⁿ; R) ≅ R for even k ≤ 2n, and H_k(ℂPⁿ; R) = 0 for odd k and for k > 2n (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §2.2).

name: Zero Gromov–Wasserstein distance is weak isomorphism
text: two measured kernels on standard Borel probability spaces have Gromov–Wasserstein distance zero, for any exponent 0 < p ≤ ∞, exactly when they are weakly isomorphic, the converse of the pullback invariance in the earlier definition (Bauer–Mémoli–Needham–Nishino, *The Z-Gromov–Wasserstein distance*, 2025).

name: Toeplitz operators
text: for a bounded symbol a on the circle, T_a = P M_a|H² on the Hardy space, a bounded linear map in a with matrix entries ⟨e_i, T_a e_j⟩ = â(i − j), adjoint T_ā, and ‖T_a‖ ≤ ‖a‖_∞ (Conway, *A Course in Functional Analysis*).

name: The Levi form
text: for a C² real function f on a complex vector space, the Hermitian form whose matrix in holomorphic coordinates is (∂²f/∂z_j∂z̄_k), with sum, product and composition rules and the invariance L(f ∘ g)(v, w) = Lf(Dg·v, Dg·w) under holomorphic g (Hörmander, *An Introduction to Complex Analysis in Several Variables*, Ch. II).

name: Kneser neighbours
text: integral lattices L and M on one rational quadratic space are p-neighbours when their intersection has index p in each; neighbours have equal determinants and, for p ∤ 2 det L, the same genus (Kneser–Scharlau, *Quadratische Formen*, §28).

name: Weyl's complete reducibility theorem for semisimple algebraic groups
text: every finite-dimensional rational representation of a semisimple affine group over a field of characteristic zero is completely reducible, now for every semisimple group rather than those with nondegenerate Killing form (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Ch. 22).

name: The bipolar theorem
text: in a real or complex locally convex space, the bipolar of any set A is the closed absolutely convex hull of A ∪ {0}; also being formalised in mathlib4#26345 (Megginson, *An Introduction to Banach Space Theory*, §2.6).

name: The Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality on Lipschitz domains
text: for a bounded connected Lipschitz domain Ω and 1 ≤ p < ∞, ‖u − ⨍_Ω u‖_{Lᵖ(Ω)} ≤ C ‖∇u‖_{Lᵖ(Ω)} for every u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω), now for Sobolev functions on Lipschitz domains rather than C¹ functions on convex ones (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §5.8.1, Thm 1).

name: Hensel's lemma with an estimate
text: over a Henselian discrete valuation ring, if v(F(y₀)) > 2 v(F′(y₀)) then F has a unique root z with v(z − y₀) > v(F′(y₀)), and v(F(y₀)) = v(F′(y₀)) + v(z − y₀); Mathlib has this over ℤ_p (Serre, *Local Fields*, Ch. II §4).

name: Kronecker's theorem for heights
text: a point of projective space with algebraic coordinates has absolute height 1 exactly when every ratio of two nonzero coordinates is a root of unity (Bombieri–Gubler, *Heights in Diophantine Geometry*, Thm 1.5.9).

name: The isodiametric inequality
text: a bounded set in n-dimensional Euclidean space has Lebesgue outer measure at most ω_n (diam s / 2)ⁿ, the volume of a ball of the same diameter (Evans–Gariepy, *Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions*, §2.2).

name: The Mackey formula for tensor induction
text: for subgroups U, V ≤ G and a representation ρ of U, the restriction to V of the tensor induction ⊗Ind_U^G ρ is the tensor product over the double cosets VsU of the tensor inductions from V ∩ sUs⁻¹ of the conjugates ρˢ (Evens 1963, §6.2).

name: The Weyl tensor, the Schouten tensor and the Kulkarni–Nomizu product
text: for a connection on a Riemannian manifold, P = (Ric − Scal·g/(2(n−1)))/(n−2) and W = Rm − P ⊙ g, with the curvature symmetries, the first Bianchi identity, trace-freeness and vanishing on constant-curvature spaces (Besse, *Einstein Manifolds*, §1.G).

name: Perimeter and total variation by duality
text: |Du|(Ω) = sup{∫_Ω u div φ : φ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω, ℝⁿ), ‖φ‖ ≤ 1} and De Giorgi's perimeter P(E; Ω) = |D𝟙_E|(Ω), with locality, lower semicontinuity under L¹_loc convergence and |Du|(Ω) ≤ ∫_Ω ‖∇u‖ for weakly differentiable u (Maggi, *Sets of Finite Perimeter and Geometric Variational Problems*, §12.1).

name: Ore extensions
text: the skew polynomial ring R[X; σ, δ] of an algebra endomorphism σ and a σ-derivation δ, with its monomial basis, the relation Xa = σ(a)X + δ(a) and its universal property (Cohn, *Free Rings and Their Relations*, Ch. 2).

name: Connes' operator B
text: on the Hochschild cochains of a unital algebra, the cyclic operator λ, the cyclic norm N, the bar coboundary b′ and B = N s (1 − λ), with B² = 0 and bB + Bb = 0, the (b, B) mixed complex of cyclic cohomology (Loday, *Cyclic Homology*, §2.1).

name: Pivotal categories
text: a rigid monoidal category with a monoidal isomorphism X ≅ X^{∗∗}, with the Freyd–Yetter identity, left and right traces and dimensions, and the torsor of pivotal structures under Aut_⊗(𝟭); also being formalised in mathlib4#42150 (Etingof–Gelaki–Nikshych–Ostrik, *Tensor Categories*, §4.7).

name: Universally catenary rings
text: Noetherian rings all of whose finite-type algebras are catenary, stable under quotients, localisation and polynomial rings, with the criterion through polynomial rings and the local criterion over all primes (Stacks Project, Tag 00NL).

name: The S-regulator
text: the covolume of the S-unit lattice, the image of the S-logarithmic embedding, a full lattice of rank r₁ + r₂ − 1 + #S isomorphic to the S-units modulo torsion; the S-regulator is positive (Bombieri–Gubler, *Heights in Diophantine Geometry*, §1.5).

name: The smash product of pointed sets
text: X ∧ Y = (X × Y)/(X ∨ Y) makes Mathlib's category of pointed types symmetric monoidal with unit S⁰, with associator, unitors and braiding (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Ch. 0).

name: Finiteness of the Selmer group
text: for an elliptic curve E over a number field K and every m ≥ 1, the m-Selmer group Sel_m(E/K), with local conditions at the finite places, is finite; earlier updates had only m = 2 (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, X.4.2).

name: Conjugacy of Borel subgroups
text: any two Borel subgroups of an affine algebraic group of finite type over an algebraically closed field, in any characteristic, are conjugate by a rational point (Borel, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, Thm 11.1).

name: The Milman–Pettis theorem
text: every uniformly convex real Banach space is reflexive (Megginson, *An Introduction to Banach Space Theory*, Thm 5.2.15).

name: Kakutani's theorem on reflexivity
text: a normed space over ℝ or ℂ is reflexive if and only if its closed unit ball is weakly compact (Megginson, §2.6).

name: Goldstine's theorem
text: the image of the closed unit ball of a normed space under the canonical embedding into its bidual is weak-star dense in the closed unit ball of the bidual (Megginson, Thm 2.6.26).

name: James's basis criterion
text: a Banach space with a Schauder basis is reflexive if and only if the basis is both shrinking and boundedly complete (James 1950; Megginson, Thm 4.4.15).

name: The Racah–Speiser formula
text: for a semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the multiplicity of L(ν) in L(λ) ⊗ L(μ) is Σ_{w ∈ W} sgn(w) · dim L(μ)_{ν − w·λ}, where w·λ is the dot action (Humphreys, *Lie Algebras*, §24, Ex. 9).

name: The minuscule Pieri rule
text: if μ is minuscule, L(λ) ⊗ L(μ) is multiplicity-free: L(ν) occurs exactly once when ν − λ is a weight of L(μ), and not at all otherwise (Bourbaki, *Lie*, Ch. VIII §9, Ex. 2).

name: The fundamental group of the presentation complex
text: for a presentation ⟨S | R⟩, the fundamental group of its presentation complex is the presented group, the loop around the s-th circle going to the generator s (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Cor. 1.28).

name: Reductive groups are linearly reductive in characteristic zero
text: over a field of characteristic zero, a geometrically connected affine group of finite type is reductive if and only if every finite-dimensional rational representation is completely reducible (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Ch. 22).

name: Regular rings are normal
text: a regular ring that is a domain is integrally closed, so every localization of a regular ring at a prime is an integrally closed domain (Stacks Project, Tag 0567).

name: Affinoid algebras are Jacobson rings
text: over a complete nonarchimedean field K, every Tate algebra K⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩ and every affinoid algebra is a Jacobson ring: each prime ideal is an intersection of maximal ideals (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, *Non-Archimedean Analysis*, §5.2.6).

name: The Schwarz rearrangement
text: the symmetric decreasing rearrangement f* of a nonnegative function on a finite-dimensional normed space, radially non-increasing and equimeasurable with f, with the same Lᵖ seminorm for every p (Lieb–Loss, *Analysis*, §3.3).

name: The approximation property
text: the approximation, bounded approximation and metric approximation properties of a normed space, with the theorem that a Banach space with a Schauder basis has the bounded approximation property with its basis constant (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Ch. 1).

name: Hankel operators
text: the Hankel operator H_a : H² → (H²)^⊥ of an L^∞ symbol a on the circle, with H_a = 0 iff a has no negative Fourier coefficients, and the Toeplitz identity T_a T_b − T_{ab} = −H_{ā}^* H_b (Conway, *A Course in Functional Analysis*).

name: The Eilenberg swindle
text: in a preadditive category with countable coproducts, if X is a retract of Y then X ⊕ ∐_{n ∈ ℕ} Y ≅ ∐_{n ∈ ℕ} Y (Neeman, *Triangulated Categories*, §1.6).

name: Order statistics
text: the k-th order statistic of n iid real samples with cdf F has cdf Σ_{j ≥ k} C(n, j) F^j (1 − F)^{n−j}, and for uniform samples the law Beta(k, n + 1 − k) (David–Nagaraja, *Order Statistics*, §2.1).

name: Owen's T function
text: T(h, a) = (2π)⁻¹ ∫₀^a e^{−h²(1+t²)/2} / (1+t²) dt, with its symmetries, both partial derivatives and the skew-normal identity ∫_{−∞}^x 2φ(t)Φ(αt) dt = Φ(x) − 2T(x, α) (Owen 1956).

name: The logistic distribution
text: the logistic law with location m and scale s, with cdf (1 + e^{−(x−m)/s})⁻¹, its density, the quantile m + s log(u/(1−u)) and affine transport (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions*, vol. 2, Ch. 23).

name: Roth's theorem
text: for a real algebraic number α and κ > 2, only finitely many rationals ξ satisfy |ξ − α| ≤ H(ξ)^(−κ); so every real algebraic irrational has irrationality exponent two (Evertse, *Diophantine Approximation*, Thm 6.2).

name: Thue's approximation theorem
text: for a real algebraic number α of degree d ≥ 2 and κ > d/2 + 1, only finitely many rationals ξ satisfy |ξ − α| ≤ H(ξ)^(−κ) (Evertse, *Diophantine Approximation*, Thm 6.9).

name: The Bishop–Phelps theorem
text: in a real or complex Banach space, the continuous linear functionals that attain their norm on the closed unit ball are dense in the dual (Megginson, *An Introduction to Banach Space Theory*, §2.11).

name: Ekeland's variational principle
text: if φ is lower semicontinuous and bounded below on a complete metric space and ε > 0, every x admits y with φ(y) + ε·d(y, x) ≤ φ(x) and y the strict minimiser of φ + ε·d(·, y) (Phelps, *Convex Functions, Monotone Operators and Differentiability*, Ch. 3).

name: The Hardy–Littlewood rearrangement inequality
text: for nonnegative measurable f, g on a finite-dimensional real normed space with Haar measure, ∫ f g ≤ ∫ f* g*, where f* is the Schwarz rearrangement (Lieb–Loss, *Analysis*, Thm 3.4).

name: Calderón's theorem: W^{k,p}(ℝⁿ) = H^{k,p}(ℝⁿ)
text: for 1 < p < ∞ and every integer k ≥ 0, the weak-derivative Sobolev space W^{k,p}(ℝⁿ) coincides with the Bessel-potential space H^{k,p}(ℝⁿ) (Stein, *Singular Integrals and Differentiability Properties of Functions*, Ch. V §3).

name: Gantmacher's theorem
text: a bounded operator from a normed space into a Banach space is weakly compact if and only if its adjoint is weakly compact (Megginson, *An Introduction to Banach Space Theory*, §3.5).

name: The Cauchy–Binet formula
text: for p × n matrices A, B over a commutative ring, det(A Bᵀ) is the sum over p-element column sets S of det(A_S)·det(B_S), the products of corresponding maximal minors (Horn–Johnson, *Matrix Analysis*, §0.8.7).

name: Weak homotopy equivalences induce isomorphisms on singular homology
text: a weak homotopy equivalence between arbitrary topological spaces, with no CW hypothesis, induces isomorphisms Hₙ(X; k) ≅ Hₙ(Y; k) for every ring k and every n (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Prop. 4.21).

name: Classification of the finite-dimensional simple U_q(sl₂)-modules
text: at generic q, every finite-dimensional simple U_q(sl₂)-module is isomorphic to the highest-weight module L_m^ε for exactly one m ≥ 0 and sign ε (Kassel, *Quantum Groups*, §VI.3).

name: Existence of Riemannian metrics
text: every C^n real vector bundle with finite-dimensional fibres over a σ-compact Hausdorff smooth manifold carries a C^n Riemannian metric; in particular every such manifold has a Riemannian metric (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Prop. 13.3).

name: The dual of ℓ¹ is ℓ∞
text: for any index set and real or complex scalars, a ↦ (x ↦ Σ aᵢxᵢ) is an isometric isomorphism from ℓ∞ onto the continuous dual of ℓ¹ (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Ch. 1).

name: The Banach–Mazur distance
text: d(E, F) = inf ‖T‖‖T⁻¹‖ over isomorphisms T : E → F, with symmetry, the multiplicative triangle inequality, attainment in finite dimensions, and d = 1 exactly for isometric finite-dimensional spaces (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Ch. 12).

name: The modified Bessel function I_ν
text: I_ν(x) for real order ν, with its power series, positivity, derivative, the recurrence I_{ν−1} − I_{ν+1} = (2ν/x) I_ν and small-argument asymptotics; a complex version is proposed in mathlib4#43070 (DLMF §10.25).

name: The orientation double cover
text: of a real vector bundle and of a manifold, a two-sheeted covering with a free deck involution; a manifold is orientable iff the cover has a section, and a connected one iff the cover is disconnected (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Ch. 15).

name: Spherical categories
text: pivotal categories whose left and right traces agree, with the resulting trace and quantum dimension, their cyclicity, duality invariance and multiplicativity under ⊗; also being formalised in mathlib4#42191 (EGNO, *Tensor Categories*, §4.7).

name: The maximal abelian extension K^{ab}
text: the compositum of the abelian Galois subextensions of Ω/K, with Gal(K^{ab}/K) identified with the topological abelianization of Gal(Ω/K) whenever Ω/K is normal (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, *Cohomology of Number Fields*, Ch. I §1).

name: Gabriel's presentation theorem
text: every finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field is Morita equivalent to a bound quiver algebra kQ/I, with Q a finite quiver and I an admissible ideal, extending the basic-algebra case of TauCeti#16389 to all algebras (Assem–Simson–Skowroński, *Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras I*, Cor. II.3.7).

name: Krull dimension of Tate algebras
text: over a complete nonarchimedean field K the Tate algebra K⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩ has Krull dimension n, so a nonzero affinoid algebra A is finite over an embedded Tate algebra in exactly dim A variables (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, *Non-Archimedean Analysis*, §§5.2.2, 6.1.2).

name: The Thue–Roth inequality for binary forms
text: for an integer binary form F of degree d with no repeated linear factor over ℂ and κ > 2, there is c > 0 with |F(x, y)| ≥ c·max(|x|, |y|)^(d − κ) whenever F(x, y) ≠ 0 (Evertse, *Diophantine Approximation*, Thm 6.3).

name: A genus-zero curve with a rational point is the projective line
text: a regular proper curve X over k with H¹(X, 𝒪_X) = 0, k integrally closed in k(X), and a k-rational point, or any divisor of degree one, is isomorphic to ℙ¹_k over k (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Prop. 1.6.3).

name: The dual of c₀ is ℓ¹
text: for any index set ι and real or complex scalars, a ↦ (f ↦ Σᵢ aᵢ fᵢ) is an isometric isomorphism ℓ¹(ι) ≅ c₀(ι)*, so every functional Λ has norm Σᵢ |Λ(eᵢ)| (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Ch. 1).

name: Brunn's concavity principle
text: for a convex set in P × F with finite-volume fibres over P, F a d-dimensional inner product space, the d-th root of the volume of the fibre over p is a concave function of p on the projection (Schneider, *Convex Bodies*, §7.1).

name: The inclusion theorem for absolutely summing operators
text: over ℝ or ℂ, π_q(T) ≤ π_p(T) for 1 ≤ p ≤ q ≤ ∞, so every absolutely p-summing operator is absolutely q-summing, and π_∞(T) = ‖T‖ (Diestel–Jarchow–Tonge, *Absolutely Summing Operators*, Thm 2.8).

name: Cohen–Macaulay modules
text: a finite module M over a Noetherian local ring is Cohen–Macaulay when M = 0 or depth M = dim Supp M, and M is Cohen–Macaulay exactly when M/xM is, for x ∈ 𝔪 regular on M (Stacks 00N3).

name: Free independence
text: subalgebras Bᵢ are free with respect to a functional φ when φ vanishes on alternating products of centred elements from them; freeness and the restrictions of φ to the Bᵢ determine φ on the algebra they generate (Nica–Speicher, *Lectures on the Combinatorics of Free Probability*, Lecture 5).

name: Compactly supported de Rham cohomology
text: H^k_c(M), the cohomology of the complex of compactly supported smooth forms, with its comparison map to H^k_dR(M), an isomorphism for compact M, and pullback along smooth proper maps (Bott–Tu, *Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology*, §1).

name: The conductor of an abelian extension of number fields
text: the least modulus 𝔪 of K whose ray subgroup of the idele class group lies in the norm group N_{L/K}(C_L); a modulus is admissible for L/K exactly when the conductor divides it (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, Ch. V).

name: The Brauer algebra
text: B_k(δ) over any commutative ring: the free module on Brauer diagrams on k strands, multiplied by stacking with a factor δ per closed loop, of rank (2k − 1)‼ and containing the group algebra of S_k (Goodman–Wallach, *Symmetry, Representations, and Invariants*, §10.1).

name: Christoffel symbols
text: for a smooth symmetric nondegenerate metric g on an open set of ℝⁿ, the unique symmetric g-compatible bilinear map Γ, with Γ^k_ij = ½ Σ_l g^kl(∂_i g_jl + ∂_j g_il − ∂_l g_ij), the Levi-Civita connection for positive-definite g (O'Neill, *Semi-Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 3).

name: The generalized extreme-value distribution
text: GEV(m, s, ξ) with its cdf and quantile, weak continuity in the parameters including the Gumbel limit at ξ = 0, and max-stability: the maximum of n copies is GEV with scale s·n^ξ and location m + s(n^ξ − 1)/ξ (Coles, *An Introduction to Statistical Modeling of Extreme Values*, Ch. 3).

name: The generalized Pareto distribution
text: GPD(s, ξ) for every real shape, with density, cdf, quantile, the moments sⁿ n!/∏(1 − (j + 1)ξ) on nξ < 1, threshold stability for admissible thresholds, and the uniform, exponential and Pareto special cases (Coles, *An Introduction to Statistical Modeling of Extreme Values*, Ch. 4).

name: Verma modules of U_q(sl₂)
text: M(μ), the quotient of U_q(sl₂) by the left ideal (E, K − μ), with the basis F^j v₀ for q, μ ≠ 0 and the singular-vector criterion E·F^(j+1) v₀ = 0 ⟺ μ² = q^(2j) at generic q (Kassel, *Quantum Groups*, §VI.3).

name: The Poisson binomial distribution
text: the law of the number of successes in independent Bernoulli trials with probabilities pᵢ, with its mass function, generating function ∏(1 − pᵢ + pᵢ z), and the binomial case for equal pᵢ (Wang, *Statistica Sinica* 3, 1993).

name: The Skellam distribution
text: the law on ℤ of the difference of independent Poisson(r₁) and Poisson(r₂) counts, with its mass function, mean r₁ − r₂, variance r₁ + r₂, characteristic function and convolution by adding rates (Skellam, *J. Roy. Statist. Soc.* 109, 1946).

name: Solvable reductive groups are tori
text: over any field and in every characteristic, a reductive group whose geometric points form a solvable group is a torus; hence the radical of a reductive group is a central torus and its derived group is semisimple (Borel, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §11.5).

name: The Hurewicz theorem
text: for n ≥ 2 and a space with trivial homotopy groups below n, the Hurewicz homomorphism πₙ(X, x) → Hₙ(X; ℤ) is an isomorphism, now in full after the vanishing half of TauCeti#16017 (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 4.32).

name: The Poincaré lemma on manifolds
text: on a smooth manifold with boundary or corners, a C^r form of positive degree closed near a point is, near that point, the exterior derivative of a C^r form defined on all of M, extending the star-convex case of TauCeti#16833 (Lee, *Smooth Manifolds*, Thm 17.14).

name: Darboux's theorem
text: a closed C^r 2-form on an open subset of ℝⁿ, nondegenerate at x₀, is pulled back near x₀ by a C^r diffeomorphism fixing x₀ to its constant value ω(x₀) (Lang, *Fundamentals of Differential Geometry*, V Thm 8.1).

name: The second fundamental inequality
text: for every finite Galois extension L/F of number fields, H¹(Gal(L/F), C_L) = 0 and |H²(Gal(L/F), C_L)| divides [L : F], C_L the idele class group (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, VII Thm 5.1).

name: Karp's theorem
text: two structures in a relational language are potentially isomorphic, i.e. linked by a back-and-forth system of partial isomorphisms, exactly when they satisfy the same L_{∞ω} sentences; no countability is assumed (Karp 1965).

name: Kronecker's approximation theorem
text: if 1, α₁, …, αₙ are linearly independent over ℚ, then for every θ ∈ ℝⁿ and ε > 0 infinitely many integers y and x ∈ ℤⁿ satisfy |yαᵢ − xᵢ − θᵢ| ≤ ε for all i (Hardy–Wright, Thm 442).

name: The fundamental class of a compact oriented manifold
text: a compact connected oriented n-manifold M has Hₙ(M; ℤ) ≅ ℤ, generated by the fundamental class [M], the unique class restricting to the given local orientation at every point (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 3.26).

name: The Mayer–Vietoris sequence for de Rham cohomology
text: for open sets U, V of a σ-compact smooth manifold, 0 → Ω•(U ∪ V) → Ω•(U) ⊕ Ω•(V) → Ω•(U ∩ V) → 0 is a short exact sequence of de Rham complexes (Bott–Tu, Prop. 2.3).

name: Homotopy groups of spheres up to the dimension
text: πₖ(Sⁿ) = 0 for k < n, for the unit sphere of any (n+1)-dimensional real normed space, and πₙ(Sⁿ) ≅ ℤ for n ≥ 2 (Hatcher, Cor. 4.9 and 4.25).

name: The Black–Scholes formula
text: the discounted risk-neutral expectation of a European call on a lognormal asset equals sΦ(d₊) − Ke^{−rτ}Φ(d₋), with d± = (log(s/K) + (r ± σ²/2)τ)/(σ√τ) (Shreve, *Stochastic Calculus for Finance II*, §5.2.5).

name: Eilenberg's inequality
text: for f K-Lipschitz on a subset A of a metric space into an m-dimensional normed space, ∫ ℋᵗ(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dy ≤ ω_m K^m ℋ^{m+t}(A), as an upper integral with no measurability assumed (Mattila, *Geometry of Sets and Measures*, Thm 7.7).

name: Preprojective algebras are finite-dimensional exactly in Dynkin type
text: for a connected finite graph on at least two vertices and any orientation, the preprojective algebra is finite-dimensional iff the graph is of type A, D or E, completing the non-Dynkin direction of TauCeti#8970 (Reiten, *Notices AMS* 44, 1997).

name: Prékopa's theorem
text: the marginal x ↦ ∫ f(x, y) dy of a measurable log-concave function f ≥ 0 on ℝⁿ × ℝᵐ is log-concave (Prékopa, *Acta Sci. Math.* 34, 1973).

name: The Bhatia–Davis–McIntosh bound
text: if the spectra of self-adjoint operators A, B on finite-dimensional inner product spaces are at distance ≥ δ, then δ‖X‖ ≤ (π/2)‖AX − XB‖ for every unitarily invariant seminorm (Bhatia, *Matrix Analysis*, §VII.2).

name: Milnor's homogeneity lemma
text: on a connected manifold without boundary, any point is carried to any other by a smooth isotopy of diffeomorphisms starting at the identity and fixed outside a compact set (Milnor, *Topology from the Differentiable Viewpoint*, §4).

name: Normal schemes
text: schemes whose local rings are all integrally closed domains; normality is local, normal schemes are reduced, and a locally noetherian normal scheme has discrete valuation rings at its codimension-one points (Stacks Project, Tag 033H).

name: Projection-valued measures
text: countably additive assignments of orthogonal projections on a Hilbert space to measurable sets, normalised to the identity, with the scalar measures E ↦ ⟨P(E)x, x⟩ (Reed–Simon I, §VII.2).

name: KMS states
text: for a strongly continuous ℝ-action on a C*-algebra and inverse temperature β, the states whose correlations ω(a αₜ(b)) continue analytically across a strip of width β to ω(αₜ(b) a); the 0-KMS states are the tracial states (Bratteli–Robinson II, Def. 5.3.1).

name: Reidemeister torsion
text: the torsion of a based acyclic chain complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces, an alternating product of change-of-basis determinants, independent of the auxiliary boundary bases and lifts (Milnor, *Whitehead torsion*, §3).

name: The Wigner semicircle distribution
text: the semicircle law on [−1, 1], the limiting eigenvalue distribution of Wigner matrices, built as an affine image of Beta(3/2, 3/2), with its moments, mean 0 and variance 1/4 (Anderson–Guionnet–Zeitouni, §2.1.1).

name: Normal crystals
text: Kashiwara's crystals over a root datum: a weighted set with partial raising and lowering operators whose string lengths satisfy φᵢ − εᵢ = ⟨wt, αᵢ∨⟩, with strict morphisms and duals; seminormal in Bump–Schilling's terminology (Kashiwara, *On crystal bases*, 1995).

name: Almost-conjugate subgroups
text: Gassmann equivalence: subgroups H, K of a finite group meeting every conjugacy class in equally many elements, equivalently |(G/H)^g| = |(G/K)^g| for every g; such H and K have the same index (Perlis, *J. Number Theory* 9, 1977).

name: Pseudo-null modules
text: finitely generated modules whose localisation vanishes at every prime of height ≤ 1; over a two-dimensional noetherian local ring with finite residue field, such as ℤₚ⟦T⟧, these are exactly the finite modules (Washington, *Cyclotomic Fields*, §13.2).

name: The Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether theorem
text: for a number field K the localization map Br K → ⨁_v Br K_v over all places is injective: a central simple algebra over K that splits at every completion splits over K (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, VIII Thm 4.2).

name: Scott's isomorphism theorem
text: in a countable relational language, every countable structure M has an L_{ω₁ω} sentence that holds in a countable structure exactly when that structure is isomorphic to M (Scott 1965; Marker, *Lectures on Infinitary Model Theory*).

name: Hilbert reciprocity
text: for a, b ∈ Kˣ in a number field K, the product of the Hilbert symbols (a, b)_v over all finite and real places of K is 1, now for every number field after the ℚ case of TauCeti#16252 (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI Thm 8.1).

name: The sum formula for the local invariants of a Brauer class
text: for a number field K and every x ∈ Br K, the local invariants inv_v(x) ∈ ℚ/ℤ sum to zero over all places of K (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, VIII Thm 4.2).

name: Vaaler's cube-slicing theorem
text: every central section of the cube [−1, 1]ⁿ by a k-dimensional subspace V of ℝⁿ has k-dimensional volume at least 2ᵏ (Vaaler, *Pacific J. Math.* 83, 1979).

name: Osgood's lemma
text: a function of finitely many complex variables that is continuous on an open set and holomorphic in each variable separately is analytic there (Hörmander, *An Introduction to Complex Analysis in Several Variables*, §2.2).

name: Complete reducibility for U_q(sl₂)
text: for q ∈ ℂ nonzero and not a root of unity, every finite-dimensional module over the quantum group U_q(sl₂) is semisimple (Kassel, *Quantum Groups*, Ch. VII).

name: The dimension formula for flat morphisms
text: for a flat morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian schemes, the codimension of a point x of X is the codimension of f(x) plus the codimension of x in its fibre (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 15.1).

name: The augmenting-path theorem
text: an s–t flow in a finite network is maximum exactly when it admits no augmenting path, exactly when its value equals the capacity of some cut separating s from t (Ford–Fulkerson, *Canad. J. Math.* 8, 1956).

name: The Lazard ring
text: ℤ[aᵢⱼ] modulo the associativity and commutativity relations of X + Y + ∑ aᵢⱼ XⁱYʲ, carrying the universal commutative formal group law: ring maps L → R correspond to commutative formal group laws over R (Ravenel, *Complex Cobordism*, A2.1).

name: Finite representability of normed spaces
text: E is finitely representable in F when every finite-dimensional subspace of E embeds in F with distortion at most 1 + ε for every ε > 0; it is transitive and matches the Banach–Mazur-distance form (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Def. 11.1.1).

name: The separating space of a linear map
text: for T : E → F between topological modules, the fibre over 0 of the closure of the graph of T, the limits of T xₙ with xₙ → 0; between Banach spaces T is continuous exactly when it is zero (Dales, *Banach Algebras and Automatic Continuity*, §5.2).

name: Moore's theorem
text: every simplicial group is a Kan complex: if the simplices of a simplicial set form groups and all face and degeneracy maps are homomorphisms, every horn has a filler (May, *Simplicial Objects in Algebraic Topology*, Thm 17.1).

name: The discriminant criterion for étaleness
text: a finite free algebra over a commutative ring A is étale exactly when the discriminant of a basis is a unit of A; over a field, exactly when the trace form is nondegenerate (Stacks, Tag 0BJF).

name: Vaaler's slicing theorem for products of balls
text: every central slice of a product of Euclidean balls of volume one has volume at least one, so a k-dimensional complex slice of the unit polydisc has volume at least πᵏ; the cube case was TauCeti#19048 (Bombieri–Gubler, *Heights in Diophantine Geometry*, Thm C.3.8).

name: Generators lift along Frattini covers of profinite groups
text: for a continuous surjection from a profinite group G whose kernel lies in Φ(G), the intersection of the maximal open subgroups, every lift of a topologically generating family of the target generates G (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, §2.8).

name: Serre's criterion for complete continuity
text: over a complete ultrametric field, a bounded operator between null-sequence spaces C₀(J) → C₀(I) is a norm limit of finite-rank operators exactly when its matrix has bounded entries and row norms tending to zero (Serre, *Publ. Math. IHÉS* 12, 1962, §3 Prop. 4).

name: Absolutely summing operators and unconditional convergence
text: a bounded operator on a Banach space is absolutely summing exactly when it sends every unconditionally convergent series to an absolutely convergent series (Diestel–Jarchow–Tonge, *Absolutely Summing Operators*, Ch. 2).

name: Newton polygons
text: for a polynomial or power series over a ring with a real additive valuation v, the lower convex envelope of the coefficient valuations n ↦ v(aₙ), with its behaviour under scaling, multiplication by Xᵏ and the substitution X ↦ cX (Cassels, *Local Fields*, Ch. 6).

name: The lattice of noncrossing partitions
text: NC(n), the partitions of n ordered points with no a < b < c < d having a, c in one block and b, d in another, is a lattice under refinement, with join the least noncrossing common coarsening (Nica–Speicher, *Lectures on the Combinatorics of Free Probability*, Lecture 9).

name: N-1 and Japanese domains
text: a domain is N-1 when its normalization is finite over it, and Japanese (N-2) when its integral closure in every finite extension of its fraction field is finite; the two agree for Noetherian domains with perfect fraction field (Stacks, Tag 032F).

name: Keller's orbit category
text: for a preadditive category D with a ℤ-shift, the category D/[n] with the objects of D and Hom(X, Y) = ⨁ⱼ Hom(X, Y⟦nj⟧), with its additive faithful projection from D and the periodicity isomorphism (Keller, *On triangulated orbit categories*, 2005, §1).

name: Concordance of positive scalar curvature metrics
text: two PSC metrics g₀, g₁ on M are concordant when some PSC metric on M × ℝ equals g₀ + dt² for t ≤ 0 and g₁ + dt² for t ≥ 1; concordance is an equivalence relation (Gromov–Lawson, *Ann. of Math.* 111, 1980).

name: The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion
text: an elliptic curve over a nonarchimedean local field has good reduction exactly when inertia acts trivially on its ℓ-adic Tate module, for any prime ℓ different from the residue characteristic (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, VII Thm 7.1).

name: Whitehead's lemmas
text: for a finite-dimensional Lie algebra L with nondegenerate Killing form in characteristic zero and a finite-dimensional L-module M, every derivation L → M is inner and every 2-cocycle is a coboundary, so H¹(L, M) = H²(L, M) = 0 (Weibel, *An Introduction to Homological Algebra*, §7.8).

name: Schur's theorem for ℓ¹
text: a weakly convergent sequence in ℓ¹(I), over ℝ or ℂ and for any index set I, converges in norm, so weak and norm convergence of sequences agree in ℓ¹ (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Thm 2.3.6).

name: Uniqueness of K(G, 1) spaces of CW type
text: two aspherical spaces of CW type are homotopy equivalent, by an equivalence inducing any prescribed isomorphism of fundamental groups up to basepoint change; in particular every K(G, 1) of CW type is homotopy equivalent to Milnor's classifying space (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 1B.8).

name: Cohen–Macaulay modules are unmixed
text: for a finite Cohen–Macaulay module M over a Noetherian local ring R, every associated prime p satisfies dim R/p = dim M, and the associated primes are exactly the minimal primes of the support, so M has no embedded primes (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 17.3).

name: The Banach indicatrix formula
text: for every continuous curve γ on [a, b] in a finite-dimensional inner product space, the total variation of γ equals the integral of the number of preimages of y against 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure, with no Lipschitz or bounded-variation hypothesis (Federer, *Geometric Measure Theory*, 2.10.13).

name: Orbits of algebraic group actions are locally closed
text: over an algebraically closed field, the orbit of a rational point under a finite-type group scheme acting on a finite-type scheme is locally closed: open in its closure, with boundary a closed set of strictly smaller dimension (Borel, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §1.8).

name: Tate algebras are unique factorisation domains
text: over a complete nonarchimedean field K, the Tate algebra K⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩ of restricted power series is a unique factorisation domain, hence integrally closed (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, *Non-Archimedean Analysis*, §5.2.6).

name: The Newton polygon of a product
text: for polynomials f and g over a ring with an additive valuation, the Newton polygon of fg is the Minkowski sum of the Newton polygons of f and g, and their multisets of finite slopes add (Koblitz, *p-adic Numbers, p-adic Analysis, and Zeta-Functions*, IV §3).

name: Morozov's lemma
text: over a field of characteristic zero, if ad e is nilpotent, [h, e] = 2e, h ≠ 0 and h ∈ [e, L], there is a unique f making (h, e, f) an sl₂-triple, with no finite-dimensionality assumed (Jacobson, *Lie Algebras*, III §11).

name: The Khovanov–Seidel braid group action
text: for any finite simple graph Γ, its Artin braid group acts on the homotopy category of graded modules over the zigzag algebra of Γ, each generator acting by tensoring with the two-term complex Pᵢ ⊗ eᵢZ → Z (Huerfano–Khovanov, *A category for the adjoint representation*, §4.6).

name: Mahler duality for measures on ℤ_p
text: over a complete ultrametric ring R with a pseudo-uniformiser, measures on ℤ_p correspond isometrically to their bounded moment sequences μ(x choose n), so the Amice transform is onto the power series with bounded coefficients; Mathlib master has the ℤ_p-coefficient case (Colmez, *Fonctions d'une variable p-adique*, §II.2).

name: The Liouville form and canonical symplectic form of a cotangent bundle
text: on the cotangent bundle T*M of a manifold with boundary or corners, the tautological one-form λ_p(v) = p(dπ v), which pulls back along any one-form α to α, and the closed nondegenerate form ω = −dλ, Σ dqᵢ ∧ dpᵢ in charts (Cannas da Silva, *Lectures on Symplectic Geometry*, §2).

name: The Cantor–Lebesgue function
text: C : ℝ → ℝ, continuous and monotone with C(0) = 0, C(1) = 1, derivative 0 almost everywhere, total variation 1 and not absolutely continuous, whose Stieltjes measure is an atomless probability measure singular to Lebesgue measure (Folland, *Real Analysis*, §1.5).

name: Nagata rings
text: a Noetherian ring R with R/p a Japanese domain for every prime p; finite algebras over Nagata rings are Nagata, and a Noetherian domain of dimension at most one is Nagata exactly when it is Japanese (Stacks, Tag 032R).

name: Parabolic subgroups of an algebraic group
text: a smooth closed subgroup of a finite-type affine group over a field that contains a Borel subgroup after base change to an algebraic closure; over an algebraically closed field, exactly the smooth subgroups with a conjugate containing a given Borel (Borel, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §11.2).

name: Automatic sequences
text: a sequence a : ℕ → Δ is k-automatic when a finite automaton with output computes a(n) from the base-k digits of n; such sequences are closed under maps and pairing, take finitely many values, and include every eventually periodic sequence (Allouche–Shallit, *Automatic Sequences*, Ch. 5).

name: Wirtinger derivatives
text: for a map g between complex normed spaces, ∂g and ∂̄g are the complex-linear and antilinear parts of its real derivative; ∂̄g = 0 when g is holomorphic, and ∂ⱼ∂̄ₖ f is the Levi form of a C² real function f (Hörmander, *An Introduction to Complex Analysis in Several Variables*, Ch. II).

name: The Monsky–Washnitzer algebra
text: the overconvergent power series R⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩†, those restricted at some radius ρ > 1; dense in and, over a field, strictly smaller than the Tate algebra, and an overconvergent series is invertible exactly when it is in the Tate algebra (Große-Klönne, *J. reine angew. Math.* 519, 2000, §1.2).

name: Regular local rings are Cohen–Macaulay
text: in a regular local ring every regular system of parameters is a regular sequence, so the depth equals the Krull dimension (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 17.8).

name: McCann's displacement convexity of internal energies
text: on ℝⁿ, if U(0) = 0 and s ↦ sⁿU(s⁻ⁿ) is convex and nonincreasing, the internal energy ∫U(dμ/dx) is convex along displacement interpolation, hence along W₂-geodesics from absolutely continuous measures (McCann 1997, Thm 2.2).

name: Wasserstein geodesics come from optimal dynamic plans
text: converse to TauCeti#14123: for 1 < p < ∞ on a complete separable X, every geodesic of P_p(X) is the marginal curve of a probability on paths carried by constant-speed geodesics with optimal endpoint coupling, and W_p^p is the least expected p-action (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Ch. 7).

name: The second cohomology of a loop algebra is one-dimensional
text: for a simple Lie algebra 𝔤 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, every 2-cocycle on 𝔤[t, t⁻¹] with trivial coefficients is a coboundary plus a multiple of the residue cocycle Res(f dg) κ(x, y), itself not a coboundary (Kac, *Infinite-Dimensional Lie Algebras*, Ch. 7).

name: The Rado graph is the unique countable graph with the extension property
text: any two countable graphs in which, for disjoint finite s and t, some vertex is adjacent to all of s and none of t are isomorphic; the Rado graph on ℕ, i < j adjacent when bit i of j is set, is one (Cameron, *The random graph*, 1997).

name: The spectrum of a completely continuous p-adic operator
text: for a completely continuous endomorphism u of c₀(I, K) over a complete nonarchimedean field, a nonzero μ lies in the spectrum of u exactly when μ⁻¹ is a zero of the Fredholm determinant det(1 − Tu) (Serre, *Endomorphismes complètement continus*, 1962, §§5–6).

name: Regular proper curves are projective
text: an integral proper curve over a field k whose local rings are discrete valuation rings, with k algebraically closed in its function field, is a closed subscheme of a projective space over k (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II.6.7).

name: The triangular decomposition of U_q(sl₂)
text: for q ≠ 0, multiplication p ⊗ r ⊗ s ↦ p(F) r(K) s(E) is a linear isomorphism ℂ[F] ⊗ ℂ[K, K⁻¹] ⊗ ℂ[E] ≃ U_q(sl₂), sending the monomial bases to the PBW basis F^a K^b E^c (Jantzen, *Lectures on Quantum Groups*, Ch. 1).

name: Bochner's linearization theorem for finite group actions
text: a finite group of invertible order acting by C¹ maps near a common fixed point is conjugate by a local chart to its derivative representation there, and an element acts trivially nearby exactly when its derivative is the identity (Bochner 1945).

name: The Picard–Queyranne theorem on minimum cuts
text: given a maximum s–t flow, the minimum cuts ordered by inclusion are order-isomorphic to the upper sets of the poset of free strongly connected components of the residual graph, so the minimum cut is unique exactly when there are none (Picard–Queyranne 1980).

name: Lazard's symmetric 2-cocycle lemma
text: over any commutative ring R and n ≥ 2, a homogeneous symmetric additive 2-cocycle of degree n is r·C_n for a unique r ∈ R, with C_n = ((X + Y)ⁿ − Xⁿ − Yⁿ)/d_n, d_n = p if n is a power of the prime p, else 1 (Ravenel, *Complex Cobordism*, App. A2.1).

name: Ricci and scalar curvature under conformal change
text: for ĝ = e^{2φ}g on an n-manifold, Ric^ĝ = Ric^g − (n − 2)(Hess φ − dφ ⊗ dφ) − (Δφ + (n − 2)|dφ|²) g and Scal^ĝ = e^{−2φ}(Scal^g − 2(n − 1)Δφ − (n − 1)(n − 2)|dφ|²), Δ = div grad (Besse, *Einstein Manifolds*, 1.159).

name: Sectional curvature determines the curvature tensor
text: two quadrilinear forms alternating in each argument pair and satisfying the first Bianchi identity agree once their values T(x, y, y, x) agree on independent pairs (6 ≠ 0), so constant sectional curvature κ forces R(w, u)v = κ(⟨u, v⟩w − ⟨w, v⟩u) (do Carmo, *Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 4, Lemma 3.3).

name: Automorphs of a binary quadratic form are the norm-one units of its order
text: for a primitive integral form f = (a, b, c) of discriminant D, the stabiliser of f in SL₂(ℤ) is the group of norm-one units of ℤ[(D + √D)/2], x + y√D acting as (x − by, −2cy; 2ay, x + by) (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §7).

name: Noncrossing partitions are counted by the Catalan numbers
text: the number of noncrossing partitions of n ordered points is the n-th Catalan number, by the recurrence on the block containing the first point (Kreweras 1972).

name: Perfectoid Tate rings
text: a complete Tate ring R with R° bounded and a pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ R° with ϖ^p dividing p and Frobenius R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p bijective; such rings are reduced, ℂ_p is perfectoid and ℚ_p is not (Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds*, Def. 3.1).

name: Polynomially convex sets
text: K ⊆ ℂⁿ is polynomially convex when it contains every z with |p(z)| ≤ sup_K |p| for all polynomials p; compact subsets of ℝⁿ are polynomially convex, and a compact polynomially convex set has polynomial polyhedron neighbourhoods in any open set (Hörmander, *Complex Analysis in Several Variables*, §2.7).

name: Carathéodory's prime ends
text: for a plane domain U, the classes of null chains, sequences of disjoint crosscuts of chordal diameter tending to zero that cut off nested subdomains, two chains being equivalent when each domain of one contains a domain of the other (Pommerenke, *Boundary Behaviour of Conformal Maps*, §2.4).

name: The idele class group is a class formation
text: for a number field K and every finite Galois layer L/F inside K̄, Tate's invariant H²(Gal(L/F), C_L) → ℚ/ℤ, the sum of the local invariants of an idelic lift, is injective with image the [L:F]-torsion, and H¹(Gal(L/F), C_L) vanishes (Tate, in Cassels–Fröhlich, *Algebraic Number Theory*, Ch. VII §11).

name: Mayer–Vietoris for compactly supported de Rham cohomology
text: on a Hausdorff σ-compact manifold, 0 → Ω_c(U ∩ V) → Ω_c(U) ⊕ Ω_c(V) → Ω_c(U ∪ V) → 0, with maps (ext, −ext) and ext + ext, is short exact, giving the long exact sequence of H_c (Bott–Tu, *Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology*, §2).

name: The comparison principle for parabolic equations on ℝⁿ
text: for linear parabolic operators P with a ≥ 0 of bounded trace, bounded drift and c bounded above, classical u, v on [0, T] × ℝⁿ with Pu ≤ Pv, u ≤ v at t = 0 and u − v bounded above satisfy u ≤ v; bounded solutions of the Cauchy problem are unique (Friedman, *Partial Differential Equations of Parabolic Type*, Ch. 2 §4).

name: The conjugacy criterion for free groups
text: two elements of a free group are conjugate exactly when the cyclic reductions of their reduced words are cyclic permutations of each other (Lyndon–Schupp, *Combinatorial Group Theory*, Ch. I).

name: The Gromov–Wasserstein space is geodesic
text: for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and a complete separable geodesic target Z, any two measured kernels modulo weak isomorphism are joined by a GW_p-geodesic, obtained by interpolating the kernels along geodesics of Z over an optimal coupling (Bauer–Mémoli–Needham–Nishino, *The Z-Gromov–Wasserstein distance*, 2025, Thm 45).

name: The simplicity criterion for Verma modules of U_q(sl₂)
text: at generic q, M(μ) is simple exactly when μ ≠ ±q^m; for μ = ±q^m its only proper nonzero submodule is generated by F^(m+1) v₀, with the signed (m+1)-dimensional simple module as quotient, sharpening the construction of TauCeti#18374 (Kassel, *Quantum Groups*, §VI.3).

name: Amenable topological groups
text: G is amenable when the bounded uniformly continuous functions on G carry a left-invariant mean; amenability passes to images under surjective continuous homomorphisms, and Mathlib has Følner filters but no definition of amenability (Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, *Kazhdan's Property (T)*, App. G).

name: The power residue symbol
text: for a number field with the n-th roots of unity and a prime P with N(P) prime to n, (x/P)ₙ is the unique n-th root of unity congruent to x^((N(P) − 1)/n) mod P, a residue-field character of order n (Ireland–Rosen, *A Classical Introduction to Modern Number Theory*, Ch. 14 §2).

name: The law of a selfadjoint element in a C*-probability space
text: for a positive functional φ on a unital C*-algebra and selfadjoint a, the unique finite measure μ_a on spectrum(a) with φ(f(a)) = ∫ f dμ_a for continuous f; its moments are φ(aⁿ) and μ_(g(a)) = g_*μ_a (Nica–Speicher, *Lectures on the Combinatorics of Free Probability*, Lecture 3).

name: Construction B
text: for a binary code C, the Construction A vectors with coordinate sum ≡ 0 mod 4 under the halved dot product, an even lattice of index 2 in Construction A for doubly even C such as the Golay code (Conway–Sloane, *Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups*, Ch. 5).

name: The negative multinomial distribution
text: the law on count vectors k ∈ ℕ^ι with mass Γ(r + Σk)/(Γ(r) ∏kᵢ!) · p₀^r ∏pᵢ^(kᵢ) for real shape r > 0 and weights p₀ + Σpᵢ = 1, built as a Gamma(r, p₀) mixture of independent Poisson counts (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Discrete Multivariate Distributions*).

name: The logarithmic distribution
text: for 0 < q < 1, the law on positive integers with mass −qᵏ/(k log(1 − q)), with generating function log(1 − qt)/log(1 − q), mean −q/((1 − q) log(1 − q)) and the matching variance (Johnson–Kemp–Kotz, *Univariate Discrete Distributions*, Ch. 7).

name: The Jacobson–Morozov theorem
text: in a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with nondegenerate Killing form over a field of characteristic zero, every nonzero ad-nilpotent element e is the nilpositive element of an sl₂-triple (h, e, f) (Jacobson, *Lie Algebras*, III §11).

name: Kostant's conjugacy theorem for sl₂-triples
text: in characteristic zero, two sl₂-triples (h, e, f) and (h′, e, f′) with the same nilpositive element are conjugate by an automorphism fixing e, in the group generated by the exp(ad y) with y ∈ ker(ad e) ∩ [e, 𝔤] (Collingwood–McGovern, Thm 3.4.10).

name: The Cauchy identity for Schur polynomials
text: for finite alphabets x and y, Σ_λ s_λ(x) s_λ(y) t^{|λ|} = ∏_{i,j} (1 − x_i y_j t)⁻¹ as power series, the degree-n part of the left side being h_n(x_i y_j) (Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, I.4 (4.3)).

name: Molien's formula
text: for a finite group G acting linearly on a finite-dimensional space M over a field in which |G| is invertible, the Hilbert series of Sym(M)^G is |G|⁻¹ Σ_g det(1 − t g)⁻¹ (Stanley 1979, Thm 2.1).

name: The Pietsch domination theorem
text: for 1 ≤ p < ∞, an operator T has absolutely p-summing norm at most C exactly when ‖Tx‖ ≤ C (∫ |f(x)|^p dν(f))^{1/p} for some regular Borel probability measure ν on the weak-* dual unit ball (Diestel–Jarchow–Tonge, Thm 2.12).

name: The Sobolev inequality for functions of bounded variation
text: on ℝⁿ with n ≥ 2, every integrable u satisfies ‖u‖_{n/(n−1)} ≤ C |Du|(ℝⁿ), extending Mathlib's inequality for compactly supported C¹ functions, with the same constant, to BV (Ambrosio–Fusco–Pallara, Thm 3.47).

name: The max-flow min-cut theorem for integer capacities
text: in a finite network with capacities in ℤd, d > 0, some flow with values in ℤd has value equal to the capacity of a cut, and every Ford–Fulkerson augmentation sequence terminates; rational capacities follow (Kleinberg–Tardos, *Algorithm Design*, §7.2).

name: Kadeishvili's intrinsic formality criterion
text: a graded algebra H over a field with HH^{n,2−n}(H, H) = 0 for all n ≥ 3 is intrinsically formal: every minimal A∞-structure with its grading and product is A∞-isomorphic to H (Keller, *Introduction to A-infinity algebras and modules*, §3.4).

name: Jørgensen's inequality for Fuchsian groups
text: for A, B in a discrete subgroup of PSL(2, ℝ) with A hyperbolic or elliptic, unless B preserves the fixed-point set of A, |tr²A − 4| + |tr[A, B] − 2| ≥ 1; the parabolic case is Shimizu's lemma (Katok, *Fuchsian Groups*, Thm 2.4.6).

name: Strassmann's theorem
text: over a complete ultrametric field, a power series converging on the closed disc of radius c whose Gauss norm is last attained at index s has at most s zeros of norm ≤ c in any complete extension field (Strassmann 1928).

name: Even unimodular overlattices of L ⊥ M are discriminant gluings
text: an even unimodular lattice containing L ⊥ M and meeting the two summands' spans in exactly L and M is the gluing of L and M along an anti-isometry q_L ≅ −q_M of discriminant forms (Nikulin 1979, Prop. 1.6.1).

name: Mittag-Leffler towers have vanishing lim¹
text: for a tower of modules A₀ ← A₁ ← ⋯ in which the images of A_k → A_n stabilise as k grows, lim¹ A_n = 0 (Weibel, *An Introduction to Homological Algebra*, Prop. 3.5.7).

name: The van der Put basis of C(ℤ_p, E)
text: every continuous f : ℤ_p → E, E a complete ultrametric normed group, is the uniform sum Σ a_n(f) e_n over indicators e_n of the balls n + p^{ℓ(n)}ℤ_p, and f ↦ (a_n(f)) is an isometry onto null sequences (Schikhof, *Ultrametric Calculus*, §62).

name: Local cohomology sheaves
text: for an abelian sheaf F and closed S ⊆ X, 𝓗_S^n(F) is the sheafification of W ↦ H^n_S(W, F); 𝓗_S⁰(F) is the sheaf of sections supported in S, the stalks vanish off S, and 𝓗_S^{n+1}(F) = 0 for flasque F (Grothendieck, *Local Cohomology*, LNM 41, §1).

name: The theta series of a lattice
text: Θ_L(τ) = Σ_{v∈L} exp(πi‖v‖²τ) for a lattice L in a finite-dimensional real normed space, with the series of a translate γ + L; both converge locally uniformly on ℍ and are holomorphic there (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII §6).

name: Free cumulants
text: κ_π = Σ_{σ≤π} μ(σ, π) φ_σ by Möbius inversion on the lattice of noncrossing partitions, κ_n = κ_{1_n}, with the moment–cumulant formula φ(a₁⋯a_n) = Σ_{π∈NC(n)} κ_π and its inverse (Nica–Speicher, *Lectures on the Combinatorics of Free Probability*, Lectures 10–11).

name: The field of meromorphic functions on a Riemann surface
text: the meromorphic functions on a connected Riemann surface X, as holomorphic maps X → ℙ¹ other than the constant ∞, form a field and a ℂ-algebra, each operation determined by its values off the poles (Forster, *Lectures on Riemann Surfaces*, §1).

name: Demazure operators
text: for a root α, D_α on ℤ[M] sends e^x to e^x + e^{x−α} + ⋯ + e^{x−mα} when m = ⟨x, α^∨⟩ ≥ 0, with (1 − e^{−α})D_α f = f − e^{−α}s_α f and D_α² = D_α (Jantzen, *Representations of Algebraic Groups*, II.14).

name: Littelmann's root operators
text: the raising and lowering operators e_α, f_α on piecewise-linear paths, reflecting the record segments of the coroot height and translating the rest by ±α, independent of the presentation of the path (Littelmann, *Ann. of Math.* 142 (1995), §1).

name: The Lévy distribution
text: the law on (m, ∞) with density √(c/2π) (x − m)^{−3/2} exp(−c/(2(x − m))), the law of m + c/Z² for a standard Gaussian Z, with cdf erfc(√(c/(2(x − m)))) and |X − m|^q integrable exactly for q < 1/2 (Nolan, *Univariate Stable Distributions*, Ch. 1).

name: The generalized normal distribution
text: the law with density p/(2sΓ(1/p)) exp(−|(x − m)/s|^p), Laplace at p = 1 and Gaussian at p = 2, with E|X − m|^q = s^q Γ((q+1)/p)/Γ(1/p) exactly for q > −1 (Nadarajah 2005).

name: Brouwer's invariance of domain
text: a map between boundaryless topological manifolds of the same finite dimension that is continuous and injective on an open set has open image, so a continuous injection is an open embedding (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 2B.3).

name: The Newton–Puiseux theorem
text: over an algebraically closed field K of characteristic zero, every nonconstant polynomial over K⸨X⸩ has a root in K⸨X^{1/n}⸩ for some n (Walker, *Algebraic Curves*, Ch. IV).

name: The coarea formula for BV functions
text: now in full: for every u locally integrable on an open set Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, |Du|(Ω) = ∫_ℝ P({u > t}; Ω) dt, both sides possibly infinite (Evans–Gariepy, *Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions*, Thm 5.9).

name: The max-flow min-cut theorem
text: in a finite network with nonnegative capacities in any linearly ordered abelian group, including ℝ, some flow has value equal to the capacity of some cut, upgrading the integer case of TauCeti#19011 (Ford–Fulkerson, *Flows in Networks*, Ch. I).

name: Noether's finiteness theorem for invariants of finite groups
text: for a finite group acting on a finite-type algebra A over a Noetherian ring, A^G is of finite type and A is a finite A^G-module; over a ℚ-algebra, A^G is generated by orbit sums of monomials of degree at most |G| (Derksen–Kemper, *Computational Invariant Theory*, Ch. 3).

name: The second Bianchi identity
text: for a smooth connection on a vector bundle and a torsion-free connection on the tangent bundle, (∇_X R)(Y, Z) + (∇_Y R)(Z, X) + (∇_Z R)(X, Y) = 0 (Lee, *Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds*, Prop 7.5).

name: The Pietsch factorization theorem
text: for 1 ≤ p < ∞ and a Banach target, π_p(T) ≤ C exactly when T = S ∘ j_p with j_p : E → Lᵖ(ν) the evaluation map for a probability measure ν on the weak-* dual ball and ‖S‖ ≤ C (Diestel–Jarchow–Tonge, Thm 2.13).

name: The relative Proj of a graded quasi-coherent algebra
text: for a scheme X and a graded 𝒪_X-algebra A with quasi-coherent components, the scheme glued from the Proj(⨁ₙ Γ(U, Aₙ)) over affine opens U, with that description over every affine open (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II §7).

name: The henselization of a pair, with its universal property
text: for a henselian pair (S, J) and a map of pairs (R, I) → (S, J), there is a unique R-algebra map from the henselization of (R, I) to S carrying the extended ideal into J (Stacks, Tag 0A02).

name: The Lusternik–Schnirelmann category
text: the least number of open sets covering a subset of X whose inclusions into X are nullhomotopic, with monotonicity, subadditivity, the deformation inequality and homotopy invariance (Cornea–Lupton–Oprea–Tanré, *Lusternik–Schnirelmann Category*, Ch. 1).

name: Successive minima of a lattice with respect to a convex body
text: λ_i(L, K) is the least t with i + 1 independent lattice vectors in tK; they are attained simultaneously, and some ℤ-basis b of L has b_i ∈ max(1, (i+1)/2) λ_i K (Cassels, *Geometry of Numbers*, Ch. V Lemma 8).

name: The matrix normal distribution
text: MN(M, U, V), whose vectorisation is N(vec M, V ⊗ U), with entry covariances U_ik V_jl, Gaussian rows and columns, transposition and affine images (Gupta–Nagar, *Matrix Variate Distributions*, Ch. 2).

name: The asymmetric Laplace distribution
text: the law of m + X − Y for independent exponentials of rates r and l, with its two-sided exponential density, characteristic function, mean and variance (Kotz–Kozubowski–Podgórski, *The Laplace Distribution and Generalizations*, Ch. 3).

name: The Lindemann–Weierstrass theorem
text: now in full: for distinct algebraic numbers α₁, …, αₙ the values e^{α₁}, …, e^{αₙ} are linearly independent over ℚ̄, so for ℚ-linearly independent algebraic αᵢ they are algebraically independent (Baker, *Transcendental Number Theory*, Ch. 1).

name: The Hasse norm theorem
text: for a cyclic extension L/K of number fields, a ∈ Kˣ is a norm from L exactly when it is a norm from K_v ⊗_K L at every finite and infinite place v (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI §4).

name: The Poisson summation formula on ℝⁿ
text: for a Schwartz function f on a Euclidean space and the lattice ℤⁿ of an orthonormal basis, Σ_{m∈ℤⁿ} f(v + m) = Σ_{m∈ℤⁿ} 𝓕f(m) e^{2πi⟨v, m⟩}, extending Mathlib's one-dimensional theorem (Stein–Weiss, *Fourier Analysis on Euclidean Spaces*, VII Cor. 2.6).

name: The Benamou–Brenier formula
text: now in full: for 1 ≤ p < ∞ on a finite-dimensional normed space, W_p(μ₀, μ₁)^p is the least value of ∫₀¹∫‖v_t‖^p dν_t dt over narrowly continuous curves of measures from μ₀ to μ₁ solving ∂_tν + div(vν) = 0 (Santambrogio, *Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians*, Thm 5.28).

name: Grothendieck's Galois correspondence for finite étale algebras
text: for a field K with separable closure Ω, A ↦ Hom_K(A, Ω) is an anti-equivalence between finite étale K-algebras and finite sets with a continuous Gal(Ω/K)-action (Lenstra, *Galois Theory for Schemes*, §2; SGA 1, V §8).

name: The fundamental theorem of pseudo-Riemannian geometry
text: a smooth nondegenerate metric of any signature on a finite-dimensional manifold has a torsion-free metric connection, and it is smooth, extending the positive-definite case already in Mathlib (O'Neill, *Semi-Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 3 Thm 11).

name: Homotopy invariance of de Rham cohomology
text: smoothly homotopic maps f, g : M → M' induce the same map H^k_dR(M') → H^k_dR(M) in every degree, with M allowed boundary and corners (Bott–Tu, *Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology*, §4).

name: The equality case of the Brunn–Minkowski inequality
text: for compact convex A, B ⊆ ℝⁿ of positive volume and c, d > 0, |cA + dB|^{1/n} = c|A|^{1/n} + d|B|^{1/n} exactly when B is a translate of a positive dilate of A (Schneider, *Convex Bodies*, Thm 7.1.1).

name: Meromorphic functions on the Riemann sphere are rational
text: the field of meromorphic functions on ℙ¹(ℂ) is ℂ(z), by evaluation of rational functions at the coordinate (Forster, *Lectures on Riemann Surfaces*, Cor. 2.9).

name: The Eisenstein–Dumas irreducibility criterion
text: over a field with an integer-valued valuation, a polynomial of degree d with nonzero constant term whose Newton polygon is one segment of slope a/d with gcd(a, d) = 1 is irreducible (Dumas 1906; Prasolov, *Polynomials*, §2.2).

name: The cyclic bicomplex computes cyclic cohomology
text: over a ring containing ℚ, the inclusion of Connes' cyclic cochain complex into column zero of the total complex of the cyclic bicomplex is a quasi-isomorphism (Loday, *Cyclic Homology*, §2.1).

name: Centralizers of diagonalizable subgroups are smooth
text: in a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over a Noetherian ring, the scheme-theoretic centralizer of the image of a diagonalizable group D(X) is smooth (SGA 3, XI Cor. 5.3).

name: The projective and injective tensor norms
text: on E ⊗ F for normed spaces, π(u) = inf Σ‖xᵢ‖‖yᵢ‖ over decompositions and ε(u) = sup{|Σ f(xᵢ)g(yᵢ)| : ‖f‖, ‖g‖ ≤ 1}; both are cross norms and ε ≤ π (Ryan, *Introduction to Tensor Products of Banach Spaces*, §§2.1, 3.1).

name: The Frobenius–Perron character of a fusion category
text: a transitive ℤ₊-ring, such as the Grothendieck ring of a fusion category, has exactly one ring homomorphism to ℝ nonnegative on the basis; it is positive there and sends a simple object to the spectral radius of its fusion matrix (Etingof–Gelaki–Nikshych–Ostrik, *Tensor Categories*, Prop. 3.3.6).

name: Complex tori
text: for a lattice L in a finite-dimensional complex vector space E, the quotient E/L is a compact connected complex Lie group with the projection a local biholomorphism (Birkenhake–Lange, *Complex Abelian Varieties*, §1.1).

name: Siegel functions
text: g_r(τ) = −e^{πi B₂(r₁)τ} e^{πi r₂(r₁−1)} (1 − q_z) ∏_{n≥1}(1 − qⁿq_z)(1 − qⁿq_z⁻¹), q_z = e^{2πi(r₁τ+r₂)}, holomorphic and nonvanishing on ℍ for r ∉ ℤ², with its translation laws in r and in τ (Kubert–Lang, *Modular Units*, Ch. 2 §1).

name: The zeta (Zipf) distribution
text: the law with mass k^{−s}/ζ(s) at k ≥ 1 for s > 1, whose m-th moment exists exactly when m < s − 1 and equals ζ(s − m)/ζ(s) (Johnson–Kemp–Kotz, *Univariate Discrete Distributions*, Ch. 11).

name: Distributions of order zero are measures
text: a distribution T on an open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ satisfies |T φ| ≤ C_K‖φ‖_∞ for test functions supported in each compact K exactly when T = ν₁ − ν₂ for regular Borel measures finite on compact sets (Hörmander, *ALPDO I*, Thm 2.1.7).

name: The Koszul complex
text: for a linear functional φ on a module M, the complex ⋯ → ⋀²M → M → R with differential the contraction by φ, with H₀(K(φ)) ≃ R/φ(M), so H₀(K(x)) ≃ R/(x₁, …, xₙ) for a finite sequence x; also being formalised in mathlib4#43708 (Stacks, Tag 0621).

name: The inverse Gaussian distribution
text: the law on (0, ∞) with density √(λ/2πx³) exp(−λ(x − μ)²/2μ²x), cdf Φ(√(λ/x)(x/μ − 1)) + e^{2λ/μ} Φ(−√(λ/x)(x/μ + 1)), and bX ∼ IG(bμ, bλ) for b > 0 (Chhikara–Folks, *The Inverse Gaussian Distribution*, 1989).

Correctly stated. ξ is badly approximable when it is irrational and there is a c > 0 with q·‖qξ‖ ≥ c for every integer q ≥ 1, ‖x‖ = |x − round x| being the distance to the nearest integer. That is the roadmap's definition (TauCetiRoadmap/DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence, §0.6, after E19, Exercise 2.7), and the usual |ξ − p/q| ≥ c/q² for every p/q. Asking for irrationality is redundant (a rational a/b fails at q = b) but harmless, and the source asks it too.

- ¬ BadlyApproximable q for q ∈ ℚ: passes, `Rat.not_badlyApproximable` ([#L81](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/DiophantineApproximation/BadlyApproximable.lean#L81))
- ¬ BadlyApproximable (liouvilleNumber 10): passes, an example ([#L304](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/DiophantineApproximation/BadlyApproximable.lean#L304))
- BadlyApproximable φ: passes, an example ([#L299](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/DiophantineApproximation/BadlyApproximable.lean#L299))

Correctly stated. For a finite set S of finite places of a number field F, the S-units have ℤ-rank r₁ + r₂ − 1 + |S|: Dirichlet's S-unit theorem (Milne, Class Field Theory, VII §4), with S counting only finite places, the infinite ones being always allowed. Mathlib's `S.unit F` is the group of x ∈ F^× with v(x) = 1 at every finite place v outside S, `NumberField.Units.rank F` is the number of infinite places less one, r₁ + r₂ − 1, and `Module.finrank ℤ` of the additive group counts its free part, the roots of unity aside, as a rank should.

No roadmap target names it, so there are no Checks to run.

Correctly stated. For an injective family u of algebraic numbers, the exponentials exp(uᵢ) are linearly independent over the algebraic numbers: the Lindemann–Weierstrass theorem in Baker's form. The scalars are `integralClosure ℚ ℂ`, which is the field of algebraic numbers in ℂ, since over ℚ integral and algebraic agree. This is the roadmap's target as it states it (TauCetiRoadmap/DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence: "for every injective family of algebraic exponents u, the family exp(uᵢ) is linearly independent over ℚ̄", after E19, Thm. 4.8).

The index type is arbitrary: for an infinite family, `LinearIndependent` asks it of every finite subfamily, the right reading. Injectivity is needed (equal exponents give equal exponentials) and is assumed.

The roadmap lists no Checks for this target.

Correctly stated. μ(ξ) = sup{p : LiouvilleWith p ξ}, in [0, ∞], where Mathlib's `LiouvilleWith p ξ` asks for a C such that infinitely many n have an integer m with ξ ≠ m/n and |ξ − m/n| < C/nᵖ. That is the roadmap's definition (TauCetiRoadmap/DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence, §0.5; Bugeaud, Def. 1.1). The constant C does not change the supremum, and exact approximants are excluded, so a rational gets 1 and not ∞. Every real is `LiouvilleWith 1`, so the supremum is never over nothing; ∞ is reached exactly at the Liouville numbers.

Checks (§0.5):
- irrationalityExponent (1/2) = 1: passes, as `irrationalityExponent_ratCast`, for every rational ([Exponent.lean#L95](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/DiophantineApproximation/Exponent.lean#L95))
- irrationalityExponent √2 = 2: not stated as such; it follows from `BadlyApproximable.irrationalityExponent_eq` ([BadlyApproximable.lean#L134](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/DiophantineApproximation/BadlyApproximable.lean#L134)) and `badlyApproximable_sqrt_two` ([#L239](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/DiophantineApproximation/BadlyApproximable.lean#L239))
- irrationalityExponent (liouvilleNumber 10) = ⊤: not stated as such; it follows from `irrationalityExponent_eq_top_iff` ([Exponent.lean#L78](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/DiophantineApproximation/Exponent.lean#L78)) and Mathlib's `liouville_liouvilleNumber`
- irrationalityExponent 0 ≠ ⊤: not stated as such; `irrationalityExponent_ratCast` gives 1.

Correctly stated. The hypothesis says that x₀ + Σ xᵢαᵢ = 0 with integers x₀, xᵢ forces them all to be 0, that is, 1, α₁, …, αₙ are linearly independent over ℚ. The conclusion is that for every θ and every ε > 0, infinitely many integer pairs (x, y) satisfy |αᵢy − xᵢ − θᵢ| ≤ ε for every i. That is the roadmap's target word for word (TauCetiRoadmap/DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence, §0.4, after E19, Thm. 2.22); ≤ ε and < ε give the same theorem, ε being arbitrary.

Remark: Hardy and Wright's form (ch. XXIII) also lets y be taken larger than any given N. This statement says nothing about the sign of y, and its docstring claims no more than it states.

Edge case: with no αᵢ (ι empty) it says ℤ is infinite, which is true.

The roadmap lists no Checks for this target.

Correctly stated. For coprime m and n, the coefficient of q^{mn} in the q-expansion of Δ is the product of those of q^m and q^n: τ(mn) = τ(m)τ(n), Mordell's theorem (Diamond and Shurman, Prop. 5.8.5; Serre, A Course in Arithmetic, VII §4). Δ is Mathlib's `ModularForm.discriminant`, η(z)²⁴ = q∏(1 − qⁿ)²⁴, normalised with τ(1) = 1, which multiplicativity needs (for cΔ it fails unless c = 1); `qExpansion 1` expands it in q = e^{2πiz}, Δ having period 1. With m or n zero, coprimality forces the other to be 1, and the statement reads 0 = 0 · 1, which is true.

Checks (TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms, "Δ at level one"):
- the prime-power recurrence τ(p^{r+2}) = τ(p)τ(p^{r+1}) − p¹¹τ(p^r): passes, `discriminant_qExpansion_coeff_prime_pow_add_two` ([DiscriminantEigenform.lean#L130](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/LevelOne/DiscriminantEigenform.lean#L130))
- T₂ acts on Δ by −24: passes, `heckeTCuspNat_discriminant_two` ([DiscriminantEigenform.lean#L142](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/LevelOne/DiscriminantEigenform.lean#L142))

Correctly stated. For every N it says ∑_{r=0}^{N−1} e^{2πi r²/N} = (1+i)/2 · (1+(−i)^N) · √N. That is Gauss's evaluation (1+i)(1+i^{−N})/2 · √N, since i^{−N} = (−i)^N: the sum is √N, 0, i√N or (1+i)√N as N ≡ 1, 2, 3 or 0 mod 4.

Edge cases: at N = 0 both sides are 0 (an empty sum, and √0), so no hypothesis N ≥ 1 is needed, and no term ever divides by 0. Both sides also agree numerically for every N < 200.

No roadmap target names it, so there are no Checks to run.

Correctly stated. `NumberField.discr K % 4 = 0 ∨ NumberField.discr K % 4 = 1` is Stickelberger's congruence, d_K ≡ 0 or 1 mod 4, for every number field K with nothing else assumed, as the roadmap asks (TauCetiRoadmap/Completed/NumberFieldArithmetic, §4.5). `NumberField.discr K` is Mathlib's absolute discriminant, and `%` on ℤ is the Euclidean remainder (`Int.emod`), so negative discriminants come out right: −4 gives 0 and −3 gives 1.

§4.5 lists no Checks beyond the statement itself.

Correctly stated, for the form it claims. Two K-algebra maps f, g : B → A, B central simple and A simple and finite-dimensional, are conjugate by a unit of A. The roadmap's target (TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SemisimpleAlgebras, Layer 5) asks A and B both central simple and finite-dimensional; this drops the centrality of A, and the finite-dimensionality of B, which follows since f is injective. So it covers the target.

It is not the classical theorem in full: that one (Pierce, ch. 12; Gille and Szamuely, ch. 2) asks the target A to be central simple and lets B be merely simple, a subfield of A say, which this statement does not cover. The roadmap defers that form, and the module docstring says so. The file's negative control shows that centrality of the source cannot simply be dropped here.
